newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans first auction of institutional shares.
newsitem.headline: China plans first auction of institutional shares.

text.p: Institutional shares in listed Chinese firms will soon be auctioned for the first time in the six-year history of China's stock markets, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
Institutional shares can be traded between institutions -- almost all of them state-controlled entities -- but currently cannot be publicly bought and sold on the stock markets.

The newspaper said the Hainan Materials Auction Market will auction institutional shares in four Shanghai-listed A share companies owned by an unnamed Shanghai investment company which has significant debts.
The Hainan People's Court ruled that the investment company must auction the shares to raise funds to pay off its debts.

The case involves 907,500 shares in Shanghai Hualian Co, 1.824 million shares in Shanghai First Provision Co, 943,800 shares in Shanghai Yuyuan Tourist Super Bazar Co and one million shares in New Asia Fast Food Co.
The newspaper said the Shanghai investment company bought the listed firms' shares on their initial public offerings and it had no business connection with the firms.
There have been many cases in which institutional shares were sold by both listed and unlisted firms but it will be the first time that such shares are auctioned, the newspaper said.
The newspaper said Chinese corporate laws and securities rules make no special provisions for the auctioning of institutional shares and the case might prompt amendments to existing regulations.
